faq.sub: Everything you need before connecting your first store. Can't find your answer? Talk to us.

items.q: What is Rioko?
items.a: Rioko automates invoicing for your online sales. It connects Shopify or Stripe to your certified invoicing software (InvoiceXpress, Moloni or Vendus) and issues an invoice for every order automatically, with no manual work.

items.q: Which platforms does it work with?
items.a: Payment sources: Shopify, Stripe and Lodgify, all available today (EuPago and Easypay coming soon). Invoicing software: InvoiceXpress, Moloni and Vendus, all available today. Each store connects only the integrations it needs.

items.q: Are the invoices legal and certified in Portugal?
items.a: Yes. Rioko doesn't issue invoices itself; it sends the data to your AT-certified software (InvoiceXpress, Moloni or Vendus), which issues the document with ATCUD, a reported series and the correct VAT exemptions (M01–M99). The certification is the invoicing software's.

items.q: Do I need to install a checkout extension on Shopify?
items.a: No. Rioko connects via webhook and API, with no extensions and no changes to your checkout. You set it up once in the dashboard and it invoices on its own.

items.q: How much does Rioko cost?
items.a: €7.50 + VAT per month or €75 + VAT per year, per connected integration (two months free on the annual plan). No per-document fees and no volume limits. Custom integrations (ERP, marketplaces) are quoted case by case.

items.q: How long does setup take?
items.a: About four minutes: connect the store, pick the invoicing software and series, and activate. No card required to start.

items.q: How does Rioko handle NIF, VAT and foreign sales?
items.a: Rioko detects the customer's tax ID, applies the correct VAT rate and flags exempt or intra-EU sales (reverse charge, OSS). The billing address determines the country and the rate applied to each document.

items.q: How does automatic invoicing work on Shopify?
items.a: When an order is paid, Shopify sends a webhook to Rioko. Rioko validates the data, detects the VAT ID, calculates VAT and sends everything to your certified invoicing program (InvoiceXpress, Moloni or Vendus), which issues the invoice, usually in under a second.

items.q: Do I need to install an app or checkout extension?
items.a: No. Rioko connects via webhook and API: it installs nothing in your theme, doesn't touch the checkout and doesn't slow the store down. You configure it once in the panel and it keeps invoicing on its own.

items.q: Does it work with InvoiceXpress, Moloni and Vendus?
items.a: Yes, all three. You pick the destination program when configuring the integration and can switch later without rebuilding the Shopify connection.

items.q: Do invoices carry ATCUD and are they accepted by the Portuguese tax authority?
items.a: Yes. Rioko doesn't issue invoices itself; it sends the data to your program certified by the tax authority (AT), which issues the document with ATCUD, a reported series and the correct VAT exemptions (M01–M99). The certification is the invoicing program's.

items.q: How is the customer's VAT ID captured?
items.a: Rioko looks for the VAT ID in note_attributes (checkout VAT apps), order notes and the billing address, and validates it algorithmically. Without a valid VAT ID, the document is issued as final consumer, as the law allows.

items.q: What about refunds and cancelled orders?
items.a: A refund on Shopify automatically generates a credit note in your invoicing program, with totals reconciled against the refunded amount, including partial refunds.

items.q: I sell with VAT included and also outside Portugal. Does it work?
items.a: Yes. Rioko supports VAT-included or VAT-on-top pricing, applies the right rate per country, and handles exemptions, reverse charge and OSS for intra-EU sales.

items.q: How much does it cost and how long does setup take?
items.a: €7.50 + VAT per month or €75 + VAT per year, per integration, with no per-document fees and no volume limits. Setup takes about four minutes and no card is needed to start.

meta.title: InvoiceXpress, Moloni or Vendus: which to pick for automatic invoicing | Rioko
meta.description: A practical comparison of the three certified Portuguese invoicing programs Rioko connects to Shopify, Stripe and Lodgify: document types, foreign currency, simplified invoices, and which one fits which case.

hero.sub: All three are invoicing programs certified by the Portuguese tax authority, and all three issue valid documents. The choice is rarely about which is best: it is about which fits your case.
hero.disclosure: Disclosure: Rioko integrates with all three and charges the same for any of them. We have no commercial preference and this page does not pick a winner.

common.title: What all three share
common.body: Before the differences, it is worth saying what does not differ. On these points the three are equivalent, which is why the choice is rarely dramatic.
common.i1Body: All three are certified by the Portuguese tax authority. The document they issue is valid, whatever the sale came from.
common.i2Body: All support series reported to the AT and stamp the ATCUD onto the document. Reporting the series is something you do once, in the program's own account.
common.i3Body: All three expose an API that allows documents to be issued by integration, which is what Rioko uses. Nothing gets installed on your site.
common.i4Body: A refund or cancellation produces the matching credit note in any of the three, partial refunds included.

table.title: Where they differ in practice
table.note: This table describes what the Rioko integration does with each program today, not each product's full feature catalog. For anything outside automatic invoicing, check with each vendor.

rows.ix: Converted to euro at the ECB rate for the date
rows.moloni: Issued in the currency paid, with native fields

choose.title: How to choose
choose.c1Title: You already use one of them
choose.c1Body: Stay with it. Your accountant already knows it, the history is already there and the series are already reported. Switching programs for the sake of automation trades a solved problem for an unsolved one.
choose.c2Title: You sell outside the euro area
choose.c2Body: Moloni is the only one of the three that, through the Rioko integration, issues in the currency actually paid using the document's native fields. With InvoiceXpress the sale is restated in euro at the ECB rate for the day. If most of your sales are in euro, this does not affect you.
choose.c3Title: You sell over the counter and online
choose.c3Body: Vendus grew up around the point of sale, so it is the most natural fit if you have a physical shop and want counter and online invoicing in one place.
choose.c4Body: If you issue many small documents to individuals, the simplified invoice saves steps, and Moloni is the one that supports it through the integration, within the legal €1,000 limit.

rioko.title: What does not change, whichever you pick
rioko.body: Rioko connects to all three the same way and charges the same for any of them: €7.50 + VAT per month or €75 + VAT per year, per integration. VAT ID detection, VAT calculation, M01–M99 exemptions, idempotency and the daily reconciliation sweep are identical in all three cases. You can also switch destination later without redoing the connection to your store or gateway.

items.q: Which is the best invoicing program for Portugal?
items.a: There is no best in the abstract. InvoiceXpress, Moloni and Vendus are all AT-certified and issue equally valid documents. The choice depends on what you already use, whether you issue in foreign currency, whether you also sell over the counter, and which document types you need.

items.q: Can I switch programs after setting up Rioko?
items.a: Yes. The destination is a setting on the integration: you change it in the dashboard without redoing the connection to Shopify, Stripe or Lodgify. Documents already issued stay where they were issued.

items.q: Does Rioko charge more for one program than another?
items.a: No. The price is per integration and identical for all three destinations. We receive no commission from any of them for this page or for any particular choice.

items.q: Do I need to report the series to the AT before starting?
items.a: Yes, and that is done in the invoicing program's account, not in Rioko. An unreported series is the single most common reason an integration stalls at launch.

items.q: Can I use two programs at once?
items.a: You can, with one integration for each. It makes sense if you invoice under different VAT IDs, or if you keep online and counter separate. Each integration is billed separately.

s2.title: 2. Data we collect
s2.body:
• Account: name, email and unique identifier (via Clerk authentication).
  • Integration credentials: tokens, API keys and webhook secrets for the platforms you connect, used only to issue tax documents on your behalf.
  • Sales data: identifier, customer, tax number, amounts, products and statuses, processed to create the invoice or credit note.
  • Technical logs: timestamps, request identifiers and external API responses, for auditing and diagnostics.

s3.title: 3. What we use it for
s3.body:
Data is used exclusively to:
  • Create Invoices, Invoice-Receipts and Credit Notes in your invoicing software automatically.
  • Ensure tax compliance (AT rules, VAT exemptions M01–M99, tax number).
  • Show history and reconciliation in the dashboard.
  • Send failure alerts and issuance reports.
  • Provide technical support when you request it.

We do not sell or share your data with third parties for marketing purposes.

s4.title: 4. Subprocessors
s4.body:
To operate the service, we rely on:
  • Cloudflare (hosting, DNS, D1, KV, Workers) — EU/global.
  • Clerk (authentication) — EU/US.
  • Shopify, Stripe, Lodgify, EuPago (sales source platforms) — according to the connection you configure.
  • InvoiceXpress, Moloni, Vendus (tax document issuers) — Portugal.
  • Stripe (processing payments for your Rioko subscription) — EU/US.
  • Resend, with MailChannels as fallback (delivery of alert and report emails) — EU/US.
  • Fly.io (fixed-IP egress relay required by Lodgify) — EU.
  • Anthropic (automatic diagnosis attached to critical alerts) — US. Only a restricted, predefined set of fields is sent: total and tax calculations, product and SKU names, the error text returned by the platform, and connection metadata. Customer name, email, tax number, order reference and user identifier are never sent.
  • Google (Google Analytics 4, anonymous traffic measurement) — EU/US, under the EU Standard Contractual Clauses. Loads only with your consent.

We use only the subprocessors required by the connection you configure. A platform you do not connect neither receives nor processes your data.

s5.title: 5. Retention
s5.body:
We keep your data while your account is active. Once the account is deleted, personal data is removed from our database within 30 days. Anonymised logs may be retained for up to 12 months for diagnostics and fraud prevention.

Tax documents already issued reside in your invoicing account and are not deleted by us: their retention follows the applicable legal archiving periods and is your responsibility.

s6.title: 6. Your rights (GDPR)
s6.body:
You have the right to:
  • Access your personal data.
  • Correct inaccurate data.
  • Request deletion ("right to be forgotten").
  • Data portability.
  • Withdraw consent at any time.
  • File a complaint with CNPD (Portuguese Data Protection Authority).

To exercise any right, email pedro@kapta.pt.

s7.title: 7. Security
s7.body: All tokens and API keys are stored encrypted. Communications between Rioko and external services use HTTPS/TLS exclusively. Incoming webhooks are cryptographically verified (for example, HMAC-SHA256 in Shopify's case) before any processing. Access to data follows the need-to-know principle.

s8.title: 8. Cookies
s8.body:
Strictly necessary (always active, no consent needed): Clerk session — authentication; rioko_impersonate_id — admin impersonation only (1 day); rioko_attr — records signup origin (referrer/campaign) for abuse prevention (90 days).

Analytics (only with your consent): Google Analytics 4 — cookies _ga and _ga_* (~2 years) measure anonymous traffic. Data may be processed by Google in the United States under the EU Standard Contractual Clauses. Loaded via Google Consent Mode v2 with analytics denied by default — these cookies are set only after you accept.

You can change or withdraw your choice at any time via Cookie settings in the page footer. Your choice is stored locally on your device for 6 months, after which we ask again. We use no marketing or advertising cookies.

s2.title: 2. The service
s2.body:
Rioko is an automatic bridge between your sales platforms and your invoicing software. Rioko sends automatic alerts when it detects issuance failures and runs a periodic reconciliation of uninvoiced sales. customInvoiceNote.label: Standing invoice note
customInvoiceNote.help: Appended to every document's observations, after the mandatory legal mentions. IX caps the field at 200 characters and truncates this first.

ixSequenceName.label: Series
ixSequenceName.help: IX series name (e.g. RVFR). Blank uses the account's default series.

ixDocumentType.label: Document type
ixDocumentType.help: invoice_receipt suits a sale already paid; invoice leaves it outstanding.

ixExemptionReason.label: Exemption reason
ixExemptionReason.help: Stamped on any 0% line (default M01). Wrong here means legally exempt documents that nobody notices.

ixB2bExemptionReason.label: B2B exemption reason
ixB2bExemptionReason.help: Used instead of the above on confirmed reverse-charge sales (default M16).

ixStampExemptionNote.label: Print the legal exemption text
ixStampExemptionNote.help: Writes the bilingual legal mention for the exemption code into observations — for carriers and customs.

ixPaymentTerm.label: Payment term (days)
ixPaymentTerm.help: Due date offset from the document date.

autoFinalize.label: Auto-finalize
autoFinalize.help: Certify the document on issue. Off leaves drafts, which can still be edited.

onlyInvoiceWhenPaid.label: Only invoice once paid
onlyInvoiceWhenPaid.help: Hold emission until the source confirms payment. On by default.

invoiceZeroTotal.label: Invoice zero-total orders
invoiceZeroTotal.help: Issue documents for fully discounted orders instead of skipping them.

posMode.label: POS mode
posMode.help: Identify a nameless buyer by VAT number instead of "Consumidor Final".

clientSync.label: Sync client records
clientSync.help: Update a generic client name in the destination when better data arrives.

ixRetentionEnabled.label: Withholding tax
ixRetentionEnabled.help: Carry a retention percentage on every document.

ixRetention.label: Withholding rate (%)
ixRetention.help: Only applied when withholding is on.

vatIncludedLegacy.label: VAT included (reverse-charge gate only)
vatIncludedLegacy.help: On this legacy path this is NOT the tax-inclusion switch: it is one of seven preconditions for B2B reverse charge. Turning it off silently disables reverse charge.

ossEnabled.label: OSS
ossEnabled.help: Required alongside reverse charge for cross-border EU B2B handling.

ossEngine.label: Per-country VAT engine (OSS)
ossEngine.help: Decides the rate from the buyer's country instead of taking it from the source: the member state's standard rate, 0% outside the EU. For B2C distance selling only — do NOT enable under a B2B reverse-charge regime, where an intra-EU sale must leave at 0%. Requires VAT-inclusive prices; otherwise the document is held as a draft with a notice.

ossExportExemptionCode.label: Non-EU exemption code
ossExportExemptionCode.help: The code stamped when the engine zero-rates a sale outside the EU. Defaults to M40.

ptRegionalRates.label: Portuguese regional rates (Madeira/Azores)
ptRegionalRates.help: Applies 22% in Madeira and 16% in the Azores instead of the mainland 23%, from the customer's postal code (DL 347/85: the rate follows the customer's domicile). Independent of the OSS engine — it can be switched on alone under a B2B reverse-charge regime. It only replaces the standard rate: a line already at 6% or 13% is left as it is.

b2bReverseChargePipeline.label: B2B reverse charge (pipeline)
b2bReverseChargePipeline.help: Invoices at 0% with a reverse-charge mention when the buyer is a business in another member state and VIES confirms it (art. 6.º n.º 6 a) CIVA + art. 196). Applies to InvoiceXpress, Moloni and Vendus. Distinct from the older reverse charge, which only works on the Shopify→InvoiceXpress path. If VIES does not answer, the document is held as a draft rather than declaring an unverified regime.

b2bReverseCharge.label: B2B reverse charge
b2bReverseCharge.help: Invoice qualifying EU B2B sales as reverse charge, after VIES confirms the buyer.

forceTaxRate.label: Force VAT rate (%)
forceTaxRate.help: Charge this rate on every product line whatever the source says — for shops whose place of supply never varies. A wrong value here misstates the VAT on every invoice. Blank means "trust the source".

ixDeriveExemption.label: Name the exemption per sale
ixDeriveExemption.help: Decides each 0% document's legal reason from the buyer's country and VAT number — export outside the EU, intra-Community supply, or the shop's own reason — instead of stamping one code on all of them. Off by default.

ixAdapterSafetyNets.label: Retry and re-read every document
ixAdapterSafetyNets.help: Creates documents through the guarded path: retries a stalled InvoiceXpress, recovers from a broken client record, sends VAT rates explicitly, and reads the document back to confirm the amounts stored. Off by default.

stripeTaxFromSource.label: Read VAT from the Stripe checkout
stripeTaxFromSource.help: Looks up the checkout session or Stripe invoice behind a payment instead of trusting the event that arrived first — the payment and charge events carry no VAT breakdown. Off by default.

stripeRoutingHints.label: Routing hints from Stripe
stripeRoutingHints.help: Lets a routing rule match how a payment reached Stripe (stripe:origin:checkout, stripe:origin:api, stripe:origin:invoice, stripe:payment_method:multibanco, stripe:description:…) and what it cost (stripe:amount:45.00, stripe:amount:eur:45.00), so money collected through different systems can be filed in different series even when they write no metadata. Name a rule 'stripe:origin:api + stripe:amount:45.00' to require both. Also reads the metadata off the Checkout Session behind a payment, so a rule matches whichever webhook arrives first. Off by default.

tagRouteByCountry.label: Route series by buyer country
tagRouteByCountry.help: Lets a routing rule named country:AU match the buyer's address, so series routing does not depend on the country being sent in metadata. Off by default.

ixRequireSeries.label: Fail when the series is missing
ixRequireSeries.help: A configured series InvoiceXpress does not know stops the sale instead of falling back to the default series. Off by default.

ixMulticurrency.label: Invoice foreign currency sales
ixMulticurrency.help: Handles sales paid in a currency other than the euro. Off by default.

vatIncludedConnection.label: Prices include VAT
vatIncludedConnection.help: Here this IS the tax-inclusion switch: it tells the destination to net the amount down when the source sent no tax breakdown.

sendEmail.label: Email the document to the buyer
sendEmail.help: Send the issued document to the customer.

exemptionReason.label: Exemption reason
exemptionReason.help: Code carried on 0% lines for this connection (default M01).

defaultVatRate.label: Default VAT rate (%)
defaultVatRate.help: Used when the payment carries no tax breakdown at all.

moloniDefaultTaxId.help: Pins one Moloni tax rule instead of resolving by rate. Wrong here misstates VAT on every line.

moloniCategoryId.label: Product category

moloniMaturityDateId.label: Payment terms

moloniPaymentMethod.label: Payment method
moloniPaymentMethod.help: Overrides the method derived from the sales channel.

moloniPartialMode.help: What to do with a deposit: nothing (off), one document per payment (instalment_invoices), or one invoice for the total plus a receipt per payment (invoice_plus_receipts).

help.pageSubtitle: How the platform works, and how to get each credential
help.pageIntro: Rioko connects a payment source (Shopify, Stripe, EuPago or Lodgify) to an invoicing platform (InvoiceXpress, Moloni or Vendus). Start with the How it works tab to see what the engine does with each sale, then open your platform's tab for the credentials.
help.thisStepByKaptaBody: The Shopify Access Token is generated and installed by Kapta's technical team during initial setup. Never share this token with anyone outside Kapta.
help.platformGeneralSub: The engine, the rules, the pages
help.generalFlowInfo: Every connection listens to your payment source. When a sale is paid, Rioko receives a signed notification, reads the sale, decides the VAT, the series and the document type, and creates the document in your invoicing software. The sale reference is stored next to the document number, and that link is what stops two documents ever existing for the same sale.
help.generalFlowStep1: The source sends a signed notification (webhook) as soon as the sale changes state.
help.generalFlowStep2: Rioko verifies the signature and ignores anything that did not come from your account.
help.generalFlowStep3: It reads the whole sale: line items, shipping, discounts, the buyer's country, VAT number and address.
help.generalFlowStep4: It decides the VAT rate per line, the exemption reason when a rate is 0%, the series and the document type.
help.generalFlowStep5: It creates the document and, with auto-finalize on, finalizes it. A refund at the source produces a credit note linked to the original document.
help.generalFlowWarn: ⚠️ One sale, one document. If the notification arrives twice, or somebody replays the event by hand, Rioko recognises the sale by its stored reference and does not duplicate it.
help.generalConnectionsInfo: A connection is a source → destination pair: Shopify → InvoiceXpress, Stripe → Moloni, Lodgify → Vendus. One account can run several connections at once, and each shows its own status on the Integrations page.
help.generalConnectionsWarn: Each connection carries its own tax settings: series, document type, exemption codes, auto-finalize, VAT regimes. Changing a setting on one connection never touches the others, even when they share the same invoicing account.
help.generalPaidInfo: By default Rioko only issues a document when the source confirms payment. Orders created but unpaid produce nothing; when the money lands, the document is issued then, dated that day.
help.generalPaidWarn: ⚠️ Shopify sends two notices per order: one on creation, one on payment. The payment notice is what closes the document. If the store never sends it (missing webhook, or a payment recorded outside Shopify), the sale stays uninvoiced until Reconciliation or the nightly sweep picks it up.
help.generalDraftsInfo: A new document starts as a draft. A draft is editable and has no fiscal value. A finalized document has its definitive number, is reported to the tax authority by your invoicing software, and is immutable: from then on the only correction is a credit note.
help.generalDraftsStep1: Auto-finalize on (recommended for e-commerce): the document is finalized within seconds, with nobody touching it.
help.generalDraftsStep2: Auto-finalize off: documents stay as drafts for review. Used when a store is starting up, still under test, or when accounting wants to look before anything is closed.
help.generalDraftsStep3: You can switch at any time. The change applies to new documents; finalized ones stay as they are.
help.generalDraftsWarn: ⚠️ In Portugal a document must be issued and reported within 5 business days. A connection left on drafts is a decision, not an oversight: if you leave it that way, somebody has to finalize the drafts in time.
help.generalTaxInfo: The regime of each sale is decided by the buyer: the country, whether they are a business with a VAT number, and what VIES answers. The part only you know is which regimes you are registered for. Each option under Tax registrations, on the connection page, authorises one of those regimes to change the VAT on your documents. All of them off keeps exactly what the source sends.
help.generalTaxStep1: Reverse charge (art. 6(6) / art. 196): sales to businesses in another Member State go out at 0% with the reverse-charge wording, after VIES confirms the buyer's VAT number. If VIES does not answer, the document stays a draft rather than declaring an unconfirmed regime.
help.generalTaxStep2: OSS: sales to consumers in another EU country carry that country's standard rate, and sales outside the EU go out at 0%. This is for distance selling to consumers, not for B2B.
help.generalTaxStep3: Madeira and the Azores: applies 22% and 16% instead of the mainland's 23%, from the customer's postcode. It only replaces the standard rate: a line already at 6% or 13% is left alone.
help.generalTaxStep4: Non-EU exemption code: the code stamped when a sale outside the EU goes out at 0%. Empty means M40.
help.generalTaxWarn: ⚠️ OSS and B2B reverse charge are different regimes and are not switched on together for the same kind of sale. Turning either on changes the VAT of documents issued from then on, and the nightly sweep re-issues the last 30 days. Check with your accountant first.
help.generalRoutingInfo: Rules that send certain sales to a different series or document type: by order tag, by buyer country, or by payment metadata. They live under Integrations → your connection → Tag routing. The first matching rule wins.
help.generalRoutingStep1: Signal: what the rule matches on (a Shopify tag, country:FR, a Stripe metadata value).
help.generalRoutingStep2: Series / document set: where that sale goes in the invoicing software.
help.generalRoutingStep3: Document type and on creation (finalize, leave as draft, or as configured on the connection): two separate fields, so a rule can change just one of them.
help.generalRoutingWarn: ⚠️ Filling in the document type and leaving on creation empty makes the rule finalize. To inherit the connection's behaviour, leave both fields empty.
help.generalReconInfo: The Reconciliation page puts the source’s sales side by side with the documents issued, so you can see at a glance what went uninvoiced and re-issue it in one click. On Shopify and Stripe connections there is also a nightly sweep that finds paid sales with no document and issues them on its own.
help.generalReconStep1: Open Reconciliation and pick the connection and the period.
help.generalReconStep2: Sales without a document are flagged, with the reason whenever Rioko knows it.
help.generalReconStep3: Issuing from there creates the document with that connection's settings, exactly as if the sale had just arrived.
help.generalReconWarn: A sale that already has a document is never issued again, by you or by the sweep: the sale ↔ document link is the defence against duplicates. If you believe a document is missing that the page says exists, talk to us before re-issuing by hand.
help.generalBillingInfo: The Billing page shows your subscription status, the charge history and Rioko's own invoices. It is also where you update the card and resume a cancelled subscription.
help.generalBillingWarn: ⚠️ While access is active Rioko issues normally. If the subscription goes inactive, issuing stops: sales keep arriving but stay uninvoiced until you settle up, after which they can be re-issued from Reconciliation.
help.generalUsersInfo: On the Users page you invite colleagues or your accountant to manage the account. The first extra user is free; each further seat unlocks for €1.50 + VAT, once. Seats are yours: removing someone frees the seat for another invite with nothing more to pay.
help.generalSupportInfo: The Dashboard shows the latest documents issued and the latest events received, with the error when there is one. Issuing failures are also emailed to you. If the error is not clear, send us the order reference and the day: we can see that document's full path.
help.connectAuthorizeInfo: With Stripe Connect there are no keys to create and no permissions to tick. You press a button, Stripe asks which account to connect, and hands you back to Rioko already connected. We ask for read access only: we just need to see the payments in order to invoice them.
help.connectAuthorizeStep1: Open Integrations and pick the Stripe Connect → your invoicing platform pair.
help.connectAuthorizeStep2: Press Connect with Stripe and sign in to the account you want invoiced.
help.connectAuthorizeStep3: Stripe returns you to this page with the account linked. There is no webhook to create: Rioko receives the events through a single platform endpoint.
help.connectAuthorizeStep4: Continue to the invoicing destination and finish the connection's tax settings.
help.connectAuthorizeWarn: 🔐 You can revoke access whenever you like, from your Stripe dashboard or the Disconnect button on the connection page. From that moment we stop invoicing that account's sales.
help.connectVsLegacyConnect: You authorise the Stripe account once. No keys, no webhook to register, nothing to renew. This is the recommended path for new accounts.
help.connectVsLegacyLegacy: You create a Restricted Key in your account and Rioko installs the webhook there. Still supported, and the path everyone already connected this way stays on.
help.connectVsLegacyWarn: ⚠️ Do not connect the same Stripe account through both paths at once. They are two separate connections and each would invoice the same sale.
help.connectDestinationInfo: Stripe Connect pairs with InvoiceXpress and Moloni. For Moloni the authorisation is also OAuth: you need your Moloni application's Developer ID and Client Secret, and you paste the callback URL the page shows you. See the Moloni tab.
help.connectDestinationWarn: ⚠️ Stripe Connect is in early access. If you do not see the card on the Integrations page, talk to us and we will enable it on your account.
help.shopifyDomainInfo: The store domain is the unique address Shopify assigned when you registered your account. It always has the form store-name.myshopify.com.
help.shopifyDomainStep4: Copy the value (without the https:// prefix) and paste it into Rioko's Domain field.
help.shopifyDomainWarn: ⚠️ Even with a custom domain (e.g. www.my-store.com), always use the .myshopify.com one here. The Shopify API rejects the custom domain.
help.shopifyTokenInfo: The Access Token is the key that lets Rioko read your store's orders. It is created in a private app inside the store, with read access to orders and customers, and Kapta generates and installs it during initial setup.
help.shopifyTokenWarn: 🔐 If the token is ever shared by mistake, revoke it immediately under Shopify Admin → Settings → Apps and sales channels → Develop apps and contact us for a new one.
help.shopifyTokenOldOrders: Orders older than 60 days — By default the Admin API only returns recent orders. To re-issue old invoices in bulk, the token needs the read_all_orders scope, which Shopify grants on request. If you see "Order #XXXX not found" for an old order, ask us to regenerate the token with that scope.
help.shopifyTokenOauthSoon: One-click install — We are moving to OAuth installation, where you authorise Rioko on Shopify like any other app, with no token to copy. Until Shopify approves our access to protected customer data, the token is still created with us.
help.shopifyWebhookInfo: Webhooks are the notices Shopify sends Rioko when an order is created, paid, edited or refunded. The Signing Secret is the key Shopify signs each notice with, and it is what lets us confirm the notice really came from your store.
help.shopifyWebhookStep1: Go to Settings → Notifications → Webhooks and press Create webhook.
help.shopifyWebhookStep2: Create four webhooks, format JSON, API version 2026-01: Order creation, Order edit, Order payment and Refund create.
help.shopifyWebhookStep3:
The URLs, in the same order, are:
  • .../webhooks/shopify/orders-created
  • .../webhooks/shopify/orders-updated
  • .../webhooks/shopify/orders-paid
  • .../webhooks/shopify/refunds-create
on the base https://shopify-invoicexpress-worker.pedrotovarporto.workers.dev. The integration page shows them ready to copy.
help.shopifyWebhookStep4: At the bottom of that same page, Shopify shows "Your webhooks will be signed with:" followed by a key.
help.shopifyWebhookStep5: Copy that key and paste it into Rioko's Webhook Signing Secret field.
help.shopifyWebhookStep6: Press Confirm Manual Install on the integration page to mark the step done.
help.shopifyWebhookInstallImageDesc: Shopify Admin → Settings → Notifications → Create webhook
help.shopifyWebhookExtra: The secret is the same for every webhook in the store: copy it once. Webhooks created by hand in the admin do not show up in Shopify's API listing, so Rioko cannot verify them on its own. That is what the manual confirmation button is for.
help.shopifyWebhookWarn: ⚠️ Without the payment webhook there are no invoices: that notice is what confirms the money. Without the refund one there are no credit notes. Check that all four ended up created and active.
help.shopifyApiVersionInfo: The "API Version" field controls which Admin API release is used. Rioko defaults to the latest version (2026-01), the same one you should pick when creating the webhooks. Only change it if Kapta tells you to.
help.stripeAccountIdInfo: The Account ID identifies your Stripe account (format acct_XXXXXXXXXXXX). Rioko uses it to make sure every webhook received belongs to your account.
help.stripeAccountIdStep2: Top left, open the account switcher (it shows the company name).
help.stripeAccountIdStep3: The Account ID appears under the name, starting with acct_.
help.stripeAccountIdStep4: Click the copy icon and paste it into Rioko's Account ID field.
help.stripeRestrictedInfo: We use a Restricted Key rather than the secret key. It reads what Rioko needs to rebuild the sale and issue the document, and the only write it asks for is creating its own webhook. It can never move money or refund on your behalf.
help.stripeRestrictedStep1: In the Stripe dashboard, open Developers → API keys → Restricted keys and press Create restricted key.
help.stripeRestrictedStep4: Set Write on Webhook Endpoints: that is what lets Rioko install the webhook for you.
help.stripeRestrictedStep5: If a Connected Permissions section exists, give Read to the same resources. Everything else stays None.
help.stripeRestrictedStep6: Press Create key, copy the value starting with rk_live_ (or rk_test_ in test mode) and paste it into Rioko.
help.stripeRestrictedWarn: 🔐 The key is shown only once. If you lose it, create a new one and revoke the old under Developers → API keys → Revoke. A missing read scope produces no visible error: it produces invoices with wrong totals or wrong VAT.
help.stripeWebhookInfo: With the Restricted Key saved, Rioko creates the webhook in your Stripe account automatically, with the right events. You only need to do it by hand if the key lacks write access on Webhook Endpoints.
help.stripeWebhookStep1: Automatic: paste the Restricted Key into Rioko and save. The webhook shows up under Developers → Webhooks seconds later.
help.stripeWebhookStep2: By hand, if needed: Developers → Webhooks → Add endpoint, with the URL https://shopify-invoicexpress-worker.pedrotovarporto.workers.dev/webhooks/stripe
help.stripeWebhookStep4: On the endpoint page, press Reveal on the Signing secret.
help.stripeWebhookStep5: Copy the value starting with whsec_ and paste it into Rioko's Webhook Secret field.
help.stripeWebhookWarn: ⚠️ One payment fires several of these events at once. That is normal and does not double up documents: Rioko recognises that they describe the same sale and keeps the first.
help.stripeTaxInfo: Unlike a storefront, a Stripe payment can arrive with no tax breakdown at all: just a total. When your account uses Stripe Tax, Rioko uses the breakdown Stripe recorded. When it does not, the rate comes from the connection's settings or from the VAT engine, depending on which regimes you have enabled.
help.stripeTaxWarn: ⚠️ If Stripe invoices are all coming out at 0%, or with VAT different from what you charged, this is where it gets fixed, not in the invoicing software. Talk to us with a payment reference to hand.
help.ixAccountInfo: The InvoiceXpress account name is your account's subdomain (e.g. company-name in company-name.app.invoicexpress.com).
help.ixAccountStep1: Sign in to the InvoiceXpress dashboard.
help.ixAccountStep2: Top right, open your account menu.
help.ixAccountStep5: If you have never enabled the API, press "Enable".
help.ixAccountStep6: The account name is in the first field. Copy it into Rioko.
help.ixApiKeyInfo: The API Key authenticates Rioko when we create invoices and receipts on your behalf. It is the only sensitive credential in this integration.
help.ixApiKeyStep1: On the same Account Preferences → API screen, copy the API Key field (the second one).
help.ixApiKeyStep2: Paste it into the matching field in Rioko.
help.ixApiKeyWarn: 🔐 The API Key can create, finalize and cancel documents in your account. Do not share it with anyone outside Kapta.
help.ixEnvProdBody: Real invoices, with fiscal value, reported to the tax authority. Use it once the store is live.
help.ixEnvSandboxBody: Test environment, no fiscal value. Technical validation before go-live only.
help.ixDocTypeInfo: Choose whether Rioko issues Invoice-Receipts (recommended for e-commerce, sale and payment in one moment) or plain Invoices (sell now, pay later, useful for B2B on terms). With plain invoices you can also set the payment term, the offset between the document date and its due date.
help.ixDocTypeWarn: ⚠️ If you pick plain Invoice, the document stays open until you issue the Receipt by hand when the customer pays.
help.ixSequenceInfo: Series split documents into numbered sequences (e.g. Web series, In-store series). Left empty, Rioko uses the account's default series. On save, Rioko checks the series actually exists in your account and warns you when the name is not found.
help.ixSequenceStep1: In InvoiceXpress → Settings → Tax authority communication → Invoicing series / ATCUD, find the series to use.
help.ixSequenceStep2: Type the exact series name into Rioko (case-sensitive).
help.ixSequenceStep3: A series in InvoiceXpress is a family: it carries a separate number per document type. New series are created in InvoiceXpress, with tax-authority reporting already enabled, never from here.
help.vatInfo: Defines how Rioko reads the prices it receives from the source. VAT Included (Shopify's default in PT): the price already contains VAT, and Rioko backs it out to get the net amount. VAT Excluded: prices arrive net and tax is added on top. Rule of thumb: a Portuguese B2C store keeps VAT Included.
help.vatWarn: ⚠️ This switch decides how a price is read, not which rate applies: the rate comes from the source or from whichever tax regimes you enabled. Wrong here, the invoice total stops matching what the customer paid.
help.autoFinalizeInfo: When a sale is paid, Rioko creates the document as a draft. With Auto-finalize on, it finalizes it right after, and reporting to the tax authority is immediate. Off, the document stays a draft and you finalize it in InvoiceXpress.
help.autoFinalizeStep1: On (recommended for e-commerce): documents finalized and reported within seconds, fully automatic.
help.autoFinalizeStep2: Off: documents wait as drafts until you confirm. Useful at launch, during testing, or in B2B with prior approval.
help.autoFinalizeStep3: You can change it at any time. It does not affect documents already finalized.
help.autoFinalizeWarn: ⚠️ In Portugal documents must be finalized and reported within 5 business days. If you turn this off, make sure somebody finalizes the drafts in time.
help.retentionInfo: Applies to services invoiced to Portuguese businesses (B2B) when the issuer is subject to withholding. On, Rioko adds the retention field to every document issued, at the percentage you set (typically 16.5% or 25% depending on the regime).
help.retentionStep1: When to enable: independent professionals (doctors, lawyers, consultants) or companies providing services to other companies subject to withholding.
help.retentionStep2: Percentage: pick the rate that applies to your activity code. When in doubt, ask your accountant: the wrong rate means tax corrections.
help.retentionStep3: When NOT to enable: B2C product e-commerce (no withholding on goods sold to consumers).
help.retentionWarn: ⚠️ Withholding changes the final invoice amount (the customer pays less and the difference is settled with the tax authority). Confirm with accounting before enabling.
help.exemptionInfo:
When an invoice has 0% VAT lines, the tax authority requires an exemption reason code. Rioko stamps the code you choose on exempt lines. Most common codes:
  • M01 — Article 16(6) of the VAT Code
  • M05 — Exempt under article 14 of the VAT Code (exports outside the EU)
  • M07 — Exempt under article 9 of the VAT Code (specific services)
  • M10 — Article 53 exemption scheme (small taxable persons)
  • M16 — Exempt under article 14 of the RITI (intra-EU B2B with a valid VAT number)
  • M40 — Reverse charge, used by default outside the EU
  • M99 — Not subject / not taxed (generic, last resort)
help.exemptionWarn: ⚠️ The wrong code is a tax offence. When in doubt, ask your accountant. The code you choose covers ordinary exempt lines; with B2B reverse charge confirmed by VIES, Rioko uses that regime's own code, and an option exists to derive the reason from each sale's actual basis (export, intra-EU, the store's own regime).
help.ixSendEmailTitle: Email the document to the buyer
help.ixSendEmailInfo: With this on, InvoiceXpress emails the finalized document to the buyer, from your account's sender and wording. Subject and body can be customised on the connection page.
help.ixSendEmailWarn: ⚠️ Only recent documents are sent: a document issued with an old date, as happens in a backfill, deliberately sends no email, so buyers do not receive invoices from months ago.
help.moloniPathsInfo: Moloni can be connected in two ways. Which one applies depends on the payment source you are connecting: the integration page already shows you the right fields.
help.moloniPathOauthBody: Used by Stripe Connect → Moloni connections. You need your Moloni application's Developer ID and Client Secret, and you paste the callback URL. No password stored, and the authorisation renews itself.
help.moloniPathPasswordBody: Used by the other connections (Shopify, Stripe Legacy, Lodgify). Besides the application, you store the username and password of the Moloni account the documents are created in.
help.moloniOauthInfo: On this path, Moloni asks whether you authorise Rioko and hands you back to the page already connected. We store no password at all.
help.moloniOauthStep1: In Moloni, open the Client Area and enable the API as a Developer. The Developer ID and Client Secret are shown there.
help.moloniOauthStep2: Copy the callback URL Rioko's page shows and paste it into your Moloni application's Redirect URI field, character for character. It is always the same URL, for every account.
help.moloniOauthStep3: Fill in the Developer ID and Client Secret in Rioko and press Authorize Moloni.
help.moloniOauthStep4: Confirm in Moloni. You come back to Rioko connected, and pick the company and document set.
help.moloniOauthWarn: ⚠️ The Redirect URI must be exactly what the page shows. One extra character, or a trailing slash, and Moloni refuses the authorisation without saying why.
help.moloniDevInfo: Moloni only allows API access through a developer account. It is free and takes 2 minutes to create.
help.moloniDevStep2: Press "Register" and use an email different from your main account's (recommended).
help.moloniDevStep3: Confirm the email and sign in to the developer panel.
help.moloniAppInfo: Each integration needs an "application" tied to your account. Moloni gives you a Client ID and a Client Secret that Rioko uses to authenticate.
help.moloniAppStep1: In the developer panel, open "My applications".
help.moloniAppStep5: Save. The Client ID and Client Secret appear in the application detail.
help.moloniAppStep6: Copy both values into Rioko (Moloni Client ID and Moloni Client Secret fields).
help.moloniAppWarn: 🔐 The Client Secret is shown only once. If you lose it, create a new application and delete the old one.
help.moloniCredsInfo: On this path Moloni uses password grant: besides the application credentials, you provide the username and password of the Moloni account where the documents should be created. Rioko encrypts these at rest and uses them only to mint short-lived access tokens.
help.moloniCredsStep1: Username: the email you sign in to moloni.pt with (not the developer one).
help.moloniCredsStep3: Company: once the credentials validate, Rioko lists the account's companies and you pick the one that issues the documents.
help.moloniCredsWarn: ⚠️ Recommended: create a dedicated Moloni user for Rioko (e.g. rioko@your-company.pt) with invoicing-only permissions. That way you can revoke the integration without touching your personal account.
help.moloniDocTypesInfo: As in InvoiceXpress, you choose between Invoice-Receipt (the e-commerce default) and plain Invoice. Moloni also supports simplified invoices. The document set is Moloni's equivalent of a series: Rioko lists your company's sets for you to pick from.
help.moloniDocTypesWarn: ⚠️ The document set and type you choose apply to everything issued on that connection, unless a tag routing rule says otherwise.
help.moloniMappingsInfo: Moloni requires one of your account's products on every document line. Rioko can map the source's items to Moloni products, and that mapping is what decides the line's VAT.
help.moloniMappingsStep2: Match each source reference to the corresponding Moloni product.
help.moloniMappingsStep3: Anything unmapped uses the connection's generic product, at whatever rate the source sends.
help.moloniMappingsWarn: ⚠️ A mapped product imposes the VAT rate it carries in Moloni, even when the source sends another. It is the right way to invoice catalogues with mixed rates (books at 6%, merchandise at 23%), and also the easiest way to stamp the wrong rate on everything.
help.eupagoHmacInfo: The HMAC Secret is the key EuPago signs every payment notification to Rioko with. Rioko uses it to verify each callback genuinely came from EuPago.
help.eupagoHmacStep1: Sign in to the EuPago back-office at backoffice.eupago.pt.
help.eupagoHmacStep3: Copy the HMAC Key shown on that page.
help.eupagoHmacStep4: Paste it into Rioko's HMAC Secret field and save. Rioko then shows the webhook URL to register.
help.eupagoHmacWarn: 🔐 The HMAC Secret must match exactly what EuPago has stored. If you rotate it at EuPago, update it in Rioko immediately: otherwise every payment notification is rejected.
help.eupagoWebhookInfo: After you save the HMAC Secret, Rioko generates a webhook URL unique to your account, ending in your identifier. Register that URL at EuPago so payment confirmations reach us.
help.eupagoApiKeyInfo: The EuPago API Key is only needed if Rioko has to call EuPago's API (for example, to fetch a payment's details). For most setups the HMAC Secret is enough: the payment data arrives in the webhook payload.
help.eupagoApiKeyHint: Leave empty unless Kapta says otherwise. The integration works without this key for standard webhook-based flows.
help.lodgifyApiKeyInfo: The API Key lets Rioko authenticate against Lodgify's API, read bookings and register a webhook endpoint for events.
help.lodgifyApiKeyStep1: Sign in to your Lodgify account.
help.lodgifyApiKeyStep3: Copy the API key shown and paste it into Rioko's Lodgify API Key field.
help.lodgifyApiKeyWarn: 🔐 Keep this key private. With it, anyone can read your properties and bookings through Lodgify's API.
help.lodgifyWebhookInfo: When you save the API key, Rioko automatically registers a Lodgify webhook for confirmed bookings (booking_status_change_confirmed) and cancelled ones (booking_status_change_declined, for refunds). No URL to enter by hand.
help.lodgifyWebhookWarn: ⚠️ Not every Lodgify key is allowed to register webhooks. If automatic registration fails, Rioko shows the URL for you to paste under Lodgify → Settings → Webhooks.
help.vendusApiKeyInfo: The API Key authenticates Rioko when creating invoices, receipts and credit notes in your Vendus account.
help.vendusApiKeyStep3: Copy the API key and paste it into Rioko's Vendus API Key field.
help.vendusApiKeyWarn: 🔐 This key authorises creating fiscal documents in your Vendus account. Do not share it with anyone outside Kapta.
help.vendusIdsInfo: Vendus requires a Register ID (the sales terminal issuing the documents) and a Series ID (the numbered sequence, e.g. 01P2026). Both are mandatory for Rioko to create valid fiscal documents.
help.vendusRegisterIdHint: In Vendus, go to Settings → Sales Terminals. The numeric ID is shown next to each terminal.
help.vendusSeriesIdHint: In Vendus, go to Settings → Invoicing Series. Use the series code (e.g. 01P2026), not the description.
help.vendusEnvInfo: Choose Production for real fiscal documents reported to the tax authority. Use Sandbox only during technical setup and testing: sandbox documents have no fiscal value.
help.footerBody: If you still have questions about setting Rioko up, our team is here to help, by email or on a scheduled call.
help.faqGeneralQ1: How long between the sale and the invoice?
help.faqGeneralA1: Seconds. The webhook arrives as soon as the source confirms payment and the document is created right after. If the source is slow to confirm (a bank reference paid the next day, say), the document is issued when that confirmation lands.
help.faqGeneralQ2: Can I pause an integration temporarily?
help.faqGeneralA2: Yes. At the top of the connection page there is an Integration active / paused toggle. While paused, webhooks keep arriving but no document is issued. When you resume, Reconciliation shows what went uninvoiced in the meantime.
help.faqGeneralQ3: A sale has no invoice. What do I do?
help.faqGeneralA3: Open Reconciliation, find the sale and issue it from there. On Shopify and Stripe connections the nightly sweep also catches most of these on its own. If it fails again, the dashboard logs say why, and you can send us the reference.
help.faqGeneralQ4: Does Rioko change documents that are already finalized?
help.faqGeneralA4: No, and it could not: a finalized document is immutable by law. Order changes after finalizing are corrected with a credit note plus a new document. While the document is still a draft, yes, it gets updated.
help.faqGeneralQ5: Can I run several integrations in the same account?
help.faqGeneralA5: Yes. Each source → destination pair is an independent connection with its own tax settings. You can run Shopify → InvoiceXpress, Stripe → InvoiceXpress and Lodgify → Moloni at the same time.
help.faqGeneralQ6: Who can access my Rioko account?
help.faqGeneralA6: You and whoever you invite on the Users page. Kapta's team can access it for support, and those accesses are logged. The credentials you store here are encrypted and never shown again once saved.
help.faqConnectQ1: What can Rioko do in my Stripe account?
help.faqConnectA1: Read the payments and the customer data needed to issue the document. It does not move money, create charges or issue refunds.
help.faqConnectA2: With the Disconnect button on the connection page, or in your Stripe dashboard under Settings → Connected apps. From that moment we stop invoicing that account's sales.
help.faqConnectQ3: Why is there no webhook for me to create?
help.faqConnectA3: With Connect, events from connected accounts arrive at a single endpoint on Rioko's side. There is no endpoint to register in your account and no signing secret to copy.
help.faqConnectQ4: I already use Stripe with a Restricted Key. Is it worth switching?
help.faqConnectA4: If it works, it is not urgent. Connect's advantage is having no key to manage and no webhook to maintain. If you do switch, disconnect the old connection first: the same Stripe account wired both ways would invoice each sale twice.
help.faqShopifyQ1: Does Rioko invoice at payment or at order creation?
help.faqShopifyA1: At payment (the orders/paid event). Order creation prepares the document, but payment is what closes it. Orders created and never paid produce no fiscal document.
help.faqShopifyQ2: How do I re-issue an invoice for an old order (over 60 days)?
help.faqShopifyA2: The Access Token needs the read_all_orders scope, which Shopify grants on request. Contact us to regenerate the token with it, then use Reconciliation to re-issue.
help.faqShopifyQ3: Does Rioko sync changes made to an order after payment?
help.faqShopifyA3: Yes, through the orders/updated webhook, and only while the document is still a draft. Once finalized, the document is immutable by law and corrections go through a credit note.
help.faqShopifyQ4: What if a customer asks for a refund in Shopify?
help.faqShopifyA4: The refunds/create webhook is picked up and Rioko issues a Credit Note in the invoicing software, linked to the original invoice. Partial refunds produce a credit note for the refunded amount only.
help.faqShopifyQ5: Can I pause the integration temporarily?
help.faqShopifyA5: Yes. The integration page has an Integration active / paused toggle. While paused, webhooks keep arriving but no document is issued until you resume.
help.faqShopifyQ6: Does the Access Token need periodic renewal?
help.faqShopifyA6: No. Shopify private-app tokens do not expire: they only stop working if revoked by hand or if the app is uninstalled from the store.
help.faqStripeQ1: Why does Rioko use a Restricted Key instead of the Secret Key?
help.faqStripeA1: Least privilege. The Restricted Key reads only the resources needed to rebuild the sale, and the only write it asks for is creating the webhook. Even if compromised, it cannot move money or change data.
help.faqStripeA2: payment_intent.succeeded, charge.succeeded, checkout.session.completed and invoice.paid describe payments and can produce a document. charge.refunded produces a credit note. Failed payments produce nothing.
help.faqStripeQ3: One payment fires three events. Do I get three invoices?
help.faqStripeA3: No. The events are recognised as describing the same sale and only the first creates the document. The rest are logged as already processed, which is normal and not an error.
help.faqStripeQ4: Can Rioko pick up the customer's VAT number from Stripe?
help.faqStripeA4: Yes, when the Stripe Customer has a Tax ID and an address. Fiscal identity lives on the Customer, not on the payment event: a one-off payment with no Customer goes out as a final consumer.
help.faqStripeA5: charge.refunded with amount_refunded < amount produces a credit note in proportion to the refunded amount, linked to the original document.
help.faqEupagoQ1: Which events does EuPago send Rioko?
help.faqEupagoA1: A PAID callback when a payment is confirmed and a REFUNDED callback when a refund is processed. Rioko answers the first with an invoice and the second with a credit note.
help.faqEupagoQ2: Do I need EuPago's API Key as well as the HMAC Secret?
help.faqEupagoA2: Not in standard setups. The payment data (amount, reference, customer) arrives in the signed webhook payload, with no outbound API call needed.
help.faqEupagoQ3: What happens if the HMAC Secret is wrong?
help.faqEupagoA3: Rioko rejects the callback with 401 Invalid signature and logs the event. No invoice is issued. Fix it by updating the HMAC Secret in Rioko to match your EuPago channel's.
help.faqEupagoQ4: Can I run EuPago and Shopify in parallel into the same invoicing account?
help.faqEupagoA4: Yes. Each source is an independent connection with its own settings, and both can issue into the same InvoiceXpress account.
help.faqLodgifyQ1: Which Lodgify events trigger an invoice?
help.faqLodgifyA1: booking_status_change_confirmed: a confirmed booking produces an invoice. booking_status_change_declined produces a credit note, if an invoice had already been issued.
help.faqLodgifyQ2: Why does Lodgify sometimes need the webhook registered by hand?
help.faqLodgifyA2: Not every Lodgify public API key may register webhooks. When yours cannot, Rioko shows the URL for you to paste under Lodgify → Settings → Webhooks.
help.faqLodgifyQ3: Does Rioko support several Lodgify properties?
help.faqLodgifyA3: Yes. All properties on the same account share the API key and run through the same connection. Use tag routing if you need different series or document types per property.
help.faqLodgifyQ4: Can I use Lodgify with Moloni or Vendus instead of InvoiceXpress?
help.faqLodgifyA4: Yes. All three exist: Lodgify → InvoiceXpress, Lodgify → Moloni and Lodgify → Vendus. You pick the combination on the Integrations page.
help.faqIxQ1: Does Rioko report invoices to the tax authority?
help.faqIxA1: Indirectly. InvoiceXpress is integrated with the tax authority and reports finalized documents automatically in Production. Rioko issues and finalizes; the fiscal reporting is InvoiceXpress's.
help.faqIxA2: It finalizes each document right after creating it, making it valid and reported. Off, the document stays a draft for manual review in InvoiceXpress.
help.faqIxQ3: How do I set up withholding tax (IRS/IRC)?
help.faqIxA3: On the connection, enable Retention and set the percentage (0 to 99.99). Rioko includes the retention field on every document. Turning it off keeps the percentage saved for later.
help.faqIxQ4: I typed the series name and Rioko says it does not exist.
help.faqIxA4: On save we check the series against your account. Confirm the exact name under Settings → Tax authority communication → Series / ATCUD. New series are created in InvoiceXpress with reporting enabled; left empty, we use the account's default series.
help.faqIxQ5: What happens if the API Key expires or is revoked?
help.faqIxA5: Requests start failing with 401, the connection is marked unauthorised and sales go uninvoiced. Generate a new key under Account Preferences → API, paste it into Rioko, and re-issue the gap from Reconciliation.
help.faqMoloniQ1: Does Moloni report to the tax authority like InvoiceXpress?
help.faqMoloniA1: Yes. Moloni is certified invoicing software and reports finalized documents automatically in Production.
help.faqMoloniQ2: Why do some connections ask for a password and others do not?
help.faqMoloniA2: Stripe Connect → Moloni connections use OAuth authorisation, with no password. The others use Moloni's password flow, which needs the username and password of the account the documents are created in.
help.faqMoloniQ3: Is it safe to store my Moloni password in Rioko?
help.faqMoloniA3: It is encrypted at rest and used only to exchange for short-lived access tokens. Even so, we recommend a dedicated Moloni user with invoicing-only permissions, so you can revoke it without touching your own account.
help.faqMoloniQ4: Can I use Moloni for intra-EU B2B reverse charge?
help.faqMoloniA4: Yes. With the reverse-charge regime enabled on the connection and the buyer's VAT number confirmed by VIES, the document goes out at 0% with the matching legal wording.
help.faqMoloniQ5: Why did a line come out with different VAT from my store's?
help.faqMoloniA5: Because the item is mapped to a Moloni product, and a mapped product imposes its own rate. That is how mixed-rate catalogues are invoiced; check the mapping if the amount is not what you expected.
help.faqVendusQ1: Does Vendus report documents to the tax authority?
help.faqVendusA1: Yes. Vendus is certified invoicing software and every document finalized in Production is reported automatically.
help.faqVendusQ2: What is the Register ID for?
help.faqVendusA2: In Vendus, every document is issued from a sales terminal. The Register ID says which terminal Rioko's documents come out of. With a single terminal, use its ID.
help.faqVendusQ3: Can I use different series for different orders?
help.faqVendusA3: Yes. Use tag routing on the connection page to send certain sales to another Series ID, based on tags, country or payment metadata.
help.faqVendusQ4: Which document types does Rioko issue in Vendus?
help.faqVendusA4: Invoice-Receipt by default, the e-commerce standard. For B2B on payment terms, switch to Invoice in the connection settings.

taxRegistrations.title: Tax registrations
taxRegistrations.subtitle: What this business is registered to do
taxRegistrations.intro: Each sale's regime is decided by the buyer: the country, whether they are a VAT-registered business, and what VIES answers. The one thing only you know is which regimes you are registered under. Each answer below authorises one of them to change the VAT on your documents; leaving them off keeps everything exactly as it is today.

reverseCharge.label: I supply services under reverse charge (art. 6.º n.º 6 / art. 196)
reverseCharge.help: Sales to businesses in another member state go out at 0% with a reverse-charge mention, once VIES confirms the buyer's VAT number. If VIES does not answer, the document is held as a draft rather than declaring an unverified regime.

oss.label: I am registered for OSS
oss.help: Sales to consumers in another EU country carry that country's standard rate, and sales outside the EU go out at 0%. For distance selling to consumers only: if your business is B2B reverse charge, this is not the one you want.

ptRegional.label: I invoice into Madeira and the Azores
ptRegional.help: Applies 22% in Madeira and 16% in the Azores instead of the mainland 23%, from the customer's postal code. It only replaces the standard rate: a line already at 6% or 13% is left as it is.

exportCode.label: Non-EU exemption code
exportCode.help: Stamped when a sale outside the EU is zero-rated. Empty uses M40.

taxRegistrations.consequence: This changes the VAT on documents issued from now on, and the nightly sweep also re-issues the last 30 days. Check with whoever does your accounting before switching it on.
taxRegistrations.consequenceMoloni: This changes the VAT on documents issued from now on, and the nightly sweep also re-issues the last 30 days. The destination countries' rates must exist in your Moloni account, or the document is refused. Check with whoever does your accounting before switching it on.
